name: Continual learning
summary: Learning from a stream of new data or tasks after deployment, without retraining from scratch and without losing what was learned before.

name: Catastrophic forgetting
summary: Training on new data overwrites weights that encoded old knowledge, so performance on earlier tasks or general skills drops sharply.

name: Stability–plasticity dilemma
summary: A model that resists change (stable) struggles to learn new things; a model that changes easily (plastic) forgets. Every continual learning method picks a point on this trade-off.

name: Loss of plasticity
summary: Networks trained for a long time on changing data gradually lose the ability to learn anything new at all (dead units, growing weights, low feature rank).

name: Replay
summary: Mix stored or regenerated old data into each new training round so the model keeps practising earlier tasks. Simple and strong, but cost grows with history.

name: Regularisation toward old weights
summary: Penalise moving parameters that mattered for earlier tasks (EWC's Fisher-weighted penalty) or penalise KL divergence from the previous model.

name: Parameter isolation and PEFT
summary: Confine updates to a small set of parameters (LoRA adapters, sparse memory slots) so most of the network is untouched.

name: The learning loop
summary: Serve, observe traces and feedback, train, evaluate, redeploy. Everything but the train step is engineering; the train step is the open problem when it repeats.

name: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
summary: Maximise likelihood of demonstration tokens. Can inject genuinely new knowledge and skills, but is off-policy and forgets when repeated.

name: Reinforcement learning (RL) for LLMs
summary: Sample the model's own outputs, score them, upweight the good ones (PPO, GRPO, RLVR). On-policy and forgets little, but can only reinforce behaviour the model already samples.

name: On-policy vs off-policy
summary: Training on the model's own samples (on-policy) vs someone else's (off-policy). Off-policy imitation suffers compounding errors on states the data never covered; DAgger is the classic fix.

name: pass@k
summary: Probability that at least one of k samples solves the task. If pass@k is near zero, RL has no reward signal to amplify.

name: Distillation
summary: Train a student on a teacher's outputs (soft logits, or for LLMs usually SFT on teacher traces). Used to warm-start RL when the student's pass@k is too low; may lower the final plateau.

name: Self-distillation and context distillation
summary: The model, given a hint or document in context, acts as its own teacher; the un-hinted model is trained to match. Closer to on-policy, so less forgetting, but the hinted teacher is biased.

name: Continual pretraining
summary: Keep pretraining an LLM on new corpora (new domains, new time periods) with LR re-warming and replay rather than training from scratch.

name: Knowledge injection
summary: Getting new facts into a model: fine-tuning, synthetic continued pretraining, editing, or simply retrieval. Fine-tuning on facts is surprisingly hard and often loses to RAG.

name: Knowledge in the weights
summary: LLMs store facts in parameters, much of it in mid-layer MLPs acting as key-value memories. Broad but no provenance, poor on the long tail, hard to update.

name: Knowledge editing
summary: Surgically change a single fact in the weights (ROME, MEMIT). Edits rarely propagate to consequences, and long edit sequences collapse the model.

name: Knowledge graphs
summary: Facts as typed entities and relations, queryable and updatable one triple at a time. The strongest form of keeping knowledge outside the weights.

name: Retrieval-augmented generation
summary: Retrieve relevant documents and put them in the prompt. The 'context' option for new knowledge: flexible and instantly updatable, but bounded by retrieval quality and context length.

name: Context engineering
summary: Deciding what goes into a model's limited context window, and how it evolves over a long agent run.

name: Agent memory
summary: Persistent stores an agent reads and writes across sessions (MemGPT-style paging, evolving playbooks). Continual learning without touching weights.

name: Test-time learning
summary: Architectures whose memory is itself updated by gradient steps during inference (TTT layers, Titans, nested learning).

name: Optimisation
summary: How weights are updated: Adam, AdamW and decoupled weight decay.

name: Transformers
summary: The attention-based architecture underneath every model in these notes.

name: Scaling laws
summary: How loss falls with parameters and data; Chinchilla's compute-optimal ratio.
